name: Dapagliflozin
route_note: oral tablet 10 mg once daily (5 mg in some diabetes regimens)

discovery.note: A C-aryl glucoside designed for metabolic stability, following the natural product phlorizin. Year of first patent filing (priority October 1999, BMS, US 6,515,117).

tagline: The first approved SGLT2 inhibitor, now used for heart failure and kidney disease
summary: Dapagliflozin was the first SGLT2 inhibitor approved anywhere (EU, 2012). Originally a glucose-lowering drug, it was shown in DAPA-HF, DAPA-CKD and DELIVER to reduce heart-failure events and kidney disease progression in people with or without diabetes.
mechanism: The sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2, gene SLC5A2) in the early proximal tubule reabsorbs about 90% of glucose filtered by the kidney. Inhibiting it causes urinary loss of roughly 60–80 g of glucose per day, lowering blood glucose independently of insulin and producing a mild calorie deficit and osmotic diuresis.

Increased sodium delivery to the macula densa restores tubuloglomerular feedback and reduces glomerular hyperfiltration, which is thought to underlie the kidney protection seen in trials. Natriuresis, lower blood pressure, a shift toward ketone use and other haemodynamic and metabolic effects are proposed to explain heart-failure benefits that occur even without diabetes.
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (adults and children 10 years and older)
Heart failure (reduced and preserved ejection fraction)
Chronic kidney disease at risk of progression

history.title: First SGLT2 approval
history.detail: The European Commission approves Forxiga in November 2012.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: After a 2012 FDA advisory committee raised bladder and breast cancer questions, FDA approves Farxiga in January 2014.

history.title: DECLARE-TIMI 58
history.detail: In 17,160 patients, dapagliflozin reduces cardiovascular death or HF hospitalisation.

history.title: DAPA-HF
history.detail: Dapagliflozin reduces worsening HF or cardiovascular death in HFrEF, including patients without diabetes.

history.title: Heart failure approval; DAPA-CKD
history.detail: FDA approves a HFrEF indication in May 2020; DAPA-CKD stops early for efficacy.

history.title: CKD approval
history.detail: FDA approves dapagliflozin for chronic kidney disease in April 2021.

history.title: DELIVER
history.detail: DELIVER shows benefit in HF with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction.

serious: necrotising fasciitis of the perineum (Fournier's gangrene)

facts: Forxiga was the world's first approved SGLT2 inhibitor (EU, November 2012).
DAPA-HF was the first trial to show an SGLT2 inhibitor benefits heart failure patients without diabetes.
